text:
### Observed differences

- The order between the activities A19, A20, A25 and the pair A26/A27 reversed. In the earlier window, A26 ran before A19 in about 31 in 100 traces (A19 first in essentially none), before A20 in about 33 in 100, and before A25 in about 36 in 100; in the later window each of A19, A20 and A25 precedes A26 in roughly 30–35 in 100 traces, with the reverse order almost never seen (0–1 in 100). The same flip holds against A27. [REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- Accordingly, these three activities moved from late to early in the case: their mean relative position was about 0.6 of the trace before and is about 0.32–0.33 in the later window, while participation changed little (A19 about 32→35 in 100 traces, A20 about 33→36, A25 about 37→31). [POS002, POS003, POS004]
- A25's late-position adjacencies disappeared: before, A27 was followed by A25 within one to two steps in about 72 traces and A25 was followed by A32 within one to two steps in about 72; afterwards these patterns survive in only about 1–2 traces. The remaining tail tightened: A27→A28 and A28→A32 are now adjacent in about 98–99 in 100 traces (before, roughly half), and A32 now follows A27 two steps later instead of three. [LAG009, LAG012, LAG008, LAG010, LAG013, LAG011]
- Activities upstream of A26 now reach it through more steps: A45→A26 went from a one-step gap in about 91 in 100 observations to gaps of two to three steps; A18→A26 from about two steps to three to four; A16→A26 from about three steps to four to five — consistent with additional activity now executing between them and A26. [LAG014, LAG005, LAG004]
- A08 became more frequent and settled into the early region: it appears in about 30 in 100 traces in the later window versus about 13 in 100 before, at a mean relative position of about 0.34 versus 0.49 with a roughly halved position spread; its order against A26 changed from mixed (about 6 vs 6.5 in 100) to consistently A08 first (about 27 vs 2.5 in 100), typically about two steps before A26 and directly before A19 in about 22 traces. [OCC001, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, LAG002, LAG001]
- A26 and A27 still occur in every trace in both windows and only drifted slightly later (mean relative position about 0.32→0.35 and 0.56→0.59). [POS005, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the ordering constraints around the A26/A27 segment changed: A19, A20 and A25, which in the earlier window executed after A26 and A27 — with A25 embedded in the late tail between A28 and A32 — now execute before A26, at about a third of the trace rather than about three-fifths. This is shown directly by the reversed pairwise orders with A26 and A27 for all three activities, corroborated by their concordant position shifts, by the loss of A25's old adjacencies (A27→A25, A28→A25, A25→A32) and by the tightening of the A27→A28→A32 tail once A25 left it. The screening context makes chance an unlikely explanation for the set as a whole: 31 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.47 expected for an unchanged process (about 60 times the chance expectation). Limitations: positions are event-order shares rather than clock time; the many agreeing items describe one underlying reorganisation rather than independent confirmations; and the evidence cannot show whether the late-execution behaviour was rescheduled within the same cases or whether an early-execution variant replaced a late-execution variant, nor why the order changed. [REL005, REL007, REL009, POS002, POS003, POS004, LAG009, LAG012, LAG008, LAG010, LAG013]

Other differences: A08 occurs in about twice as many traces as before (about 13 vs 30 in 100) and, where its order against A26 was previously mixed, it now consistently precedes A26, A27, A28 and A32; A16, A18 and A45 now sit one to two steps farther before A26 than before; and A26 and A27 themselves occur slightly later in the trace (about 0.32→0.35 and 0.56→0.59) while still appearing in every case. [OCC001, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG014, POS005, POS006]
